top_choice_rationale: P002 recognises the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, which replaced symmetry breaking with band topology as an organising principle, with a theory prediction (Kane, Mele) and a rapid, independently confirmed experimental realisation in HgTe (Molenkamp) now two decades mature. It also changed routine electronic-structure practice, since topological invariants and materials screening are now standard. The citation is scoped narrowly to the quantum spin Hall prediction and observation, which limits but does not remove the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang credit gap. P001 (Katori and Ye) has cleaner credit and is a strong, mature, independently reproduced achievement, so I rank it second ahead of no award, but its reach is extending measurement capability rather than changing the question asked of matter.
